thread:
Priya: heads up — we started seeing a sharp increase in KMS decrypt latency around 09:12 UTC, p95 climbed to ~700ms and some services retried repeatedly causing backlog
Alex_M: any error types? 503s / Throttling? sample logs?
Priya: logs show a lot of `ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded` from AWS KMS and a few `AccessDenied` spikes (likely timing with rotation). pasted snippet: `AWSKMSException: ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded`
Sara: created an incident (INC-4523) and notified oncall, tagging infra and sec teams
eng-oncall-bot: Incident INC-4523 created — priority: high — responders: eng-oncall
Matt: quick Q — did we just rotate the CMK alias in us-east-1? I saw a rotation job started at 09:08
Priya: yes, key-rotation job started as scheduled. Rotation hit ~30% of hosts at once due to concurrency bug in rollout script
Alex_M: that explains describeKey spikes + new rewrap operations. our envelope flow does: app -> fetch DEK via KMS.GenerateDataKey OR decrypt DEK; each host does that when cache miss
Priya: our DEK cache TTL is only 5m by default, so rotation + high qps => many cache misses and KMS QPS surge
Matt: mitigation proposal: (A) increase DEK cache TTL temporarily to 1h on frontends (tradeoff: longer-lived cached DEKs) (B) add exponential backoff+jitter on KMS calls (C) switch new requests to fallback alias pointing to previous key version where safe
Sara: security note: switching alias for decrypts is OK if key policy allows, but rewraps must be careful — don't re-encrypt under the old key without audit
Priya: short term actions I started: 1) deploying DEK cache TTL bump to 1h for API workers 2) enabling stronger client-side backoff (retry cap 5, base 200ms) 3) opening support case with AWS for quota spike and throttling
Alex_M: added runbook step: if KMS Throttling > 5% and p95 > 300ms, alert and consider pausing rotation rollout. Dashboards updated: /dash/kms-latency
Matt: alternative mitigation: local rewrap queue — queue failures and rewrap when KMS healthy. risk: queued ciphertexts contain DEKs/payload, must be encrypted at rest and ACL'd. Can we reuse existing DEK cache encryption for the queue?
Priya: yes, we can encrypt queue entries with tenant-scoped key and restrict access to the rewrap worker. I'll add that as follow-up, not for immediate patch
Sara: owners: Priya -> deploy cache+backoff change and coordinate with sec for alias fallback; Alex_M -> runbook + metrics + alert tuning; Matt -> prepare alias-switch script and rewrap queue design doc
eng-oncall-bot: @priya assigned INC-4523 (owner), ETA requested
Alex_M: logs grep command I used: `grep -E "ThrottlingException|KMS" /var/log/app/*.log | sed -n '1,200p'` — shared filtered output in incident thread
Priya: rolling out TTL change now, will monitor KMS error rate and request count to AWS
Matt: ops opened AWS support case ID: 1234-5678, they reported transient control-plane throttling in us-east-1 affecting CMK operations
Sara: for the postmortem, we should: 1) fix rotation rollout concurrency, 2) add pre-rotation canary to limit parallel rewraps, 3) increase DEK cache defaults, 4) document alias-fallback procedure and required audit checks, 5) test KMS degrade-mode in chaos env
Priya: noted. will also capture metrics we need: per-alias KMS calls, cache miss rate, rewrap queue depth, and key-rotate concurrency
Alex_M: thanks. quick reminder: make sure KMS calls include client-side throttling headers we added last quarter so AWS can see traffic pattern in support case
Priya: update: after TTL bump p95 down to ~180ms and throttling errors dropped by ~80% in the last 2m. continuing to monitor :thumbsup:
Sara: great. keep the incident channel updated and we'll sync on postmortem owners later
Matt: thanks team — saved us from a bigger outage.
